answer: In a garden of agents each node earns an onyx‑graded reputation token by completing verifiable tasks; the token’s weight decays quadratically with the number of identities that share it, so a sable of ten fresh IDs counts only the square‑root of a veteran’s influence. When a request arrives the protocol sums weighted tokens and rejects proposals whose effective score falls below a threshold. An attacker must buy or forge reputation for each fake ID at a cost that grows with the square of the swarm, rendering large Sybil attacks uneconomical.
